clips.caption: This is the Intro notebook for 1.1; the title cell states that the unit is about <emphasis level="strong">signals</emphasis> and the <emphasis level="strong">time axis</emphasis>.
This unit answers one question: how do we put a <emphasis level="strong">signal</emphasis> on a <emphasis level="strong">time axis</emphasis> and <emphasis level="strong">observe</emphasis> it.

First, continuous versus discrete: a <emphasis level="strong">continuous signal</emphasis> has a value at every instant; a <emphasis level="strong">discrete signal</emphasis> has values only at the <emphasis level="strong">sample times</emphasis>.

A <emphasis level="strong">discrete signal</emphasis> is described by three quantities: the <emphasis level="strong">sample index</emphasis> n, the <emphasis level="strong">sample time</emphasis> t, and the amplitude x.
The closing observation task: draw the same values with plot and with stem, and compare which drawing fits discrete <emphasis level="strong">samples</emphasis>.
